findings.description: The implementing-tasks skill frontmatter widens the App Zone (src, lib, app) from `permission: read` to `permission: read-write`. Nothing else in this diff (guard register, floor, task kinds) relates to implement-time write scope, and no cycle note, DEC row or test accompanies the escalation. The reviewing-code skill in the same diff was changed to defer to the frontmatter `zones:` block as the authority, so this key now carries more weight than before.
findings.failure_mode: If the old `read` value was the intended advisory barrier (write only through the implement gate / explicit confirmation), this silently removes the prose-level App Zone confirmation for every /implement run, including unattended run-mode runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the escalation is intentional and cite it in the commit/DEC row. If /implement is meant to write App code, keep read-write but add a line to the skill noting the implement gate remains the harness barrier; otherwise revert to `read`.

findings.cross_file_justification: floor.yaml marks 16 fence:FR-SZ* rows as floor; .claude/data/guard-origins.yaml gives every one of them `knob: LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE`, and block-destructive-bash.sh (modified in this diff) implements them but is absent from floor_files.
findings.description: The floor is defined as the set of guards no profile, knob or task may weaken, yet every floor fence (FR-SZ*, FR-SZ2*) is disabled by a single environment variable, LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE, which floor_keys does not list (it only covers .loa.config.yaml keys). The script that implements all 16 floor fences, block-destructive-bash.sh, is not in floor_files; only its corpus rows are pinned, so a regex change that still passes the pinned corpus rows but opens a new bypass shape is not caught by floor-snapshot.
findings.failure_mode: A cycle task or profile can set the env knob (e.g. via settings `env`, a wrapper, or CI) and every floor fence becomes an audited allow, with the audit row itself written to a model-writable .run/audit.jsonl. The floor then provides documentation but not enforcement.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add block-destructive-bash.sh to floor_files (and update the pin deliberately per cycle), or add an `floor_env` list naming LOA_ALLOW_STATE_ZONE_EXEC_WRITE and LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY so guard-origins.bats can assert no floor row's knob is a bare env var, and have profile-floor.bats refuse profiles that export them.

findings.description: Audit rows written by emit_block (and the FR-MERGE-2, FR-SZ and FR-SZ2 allow rows) are tagged `replay: true` whenever the environment variable LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY equals "1". The hook trusts the variable unconditionally; there is no check that the invocation actually came from the corpus runner (e.g. a BATS or run-corpus marker). The yield consumer presumably excludes replay rows from `real_blocks_30d`.
findings.failure_mode: A stale `export LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1` in a shell profile, CI job, or a settings.json `env` block causes every real block in that session to be classified as replay, so the Guards line in loa-status and the host yield under-report real blocks, and a bypass/allow-override row is also hidden from review.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a second signal before tagging replay (e.g. LOA_AUDIT_REPLAY=1 AND BATS_TEST_FILENAME set, or a nonce file the corpus runner creates under .run/), and have guard-yield.sh report the count of replay rows it dropped so a wholesale suppression is visible.

findings.description: stash-safety.md gains a `paths:` frontmatter that scopes the rule to *.sh, *.bats, .claude/scripts/** and .claude/hooks/**. Rules without `paths` are always loaded; with it, the prose guidance against `git stash … | tail` / `|| true` swallowing is only present when those file globs are being edited. The risky pattern is a Bash command, not a file edit, and is just as likely while editing markdown, YAML or application code.
findings.failure_mode: The model runs an output-swallowed stash in a session that never touched a matching path, so the rule is not in context. The harness fence FR-1.2b still catches the listed swallow shapes, but any shape outside its regex (e.g. `2>&1 | grep -v`) now has no prose backstop.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop `paths:` for stash-safety.md (keep it always-on), or widen it to `**` and rely on prompt-budget for size, since the rule guards a shell action rather than a file type.

findings.description: The inline security Red Flags list (private keys, SQL concatenation, unvalidated input, empty catch blocks, missing tests, N+1 queries) is removed from the reviewing-code prompt, leaving only a pointer to resources/REFERENCE.md. The Zone Constraints block likewise drops the explicit System Zone never-edit statement. Both appear to be prompt-budget trims unrelated to the cycle's goal.
findings.failure_mode: The review model only sees the red-flag list if it chooses to open REFERENCE.md; in budget-pressured or unattended runs the secrets/SQL/input-validation checks become optional rather than always-present, lowering review recall for exactly the categories the security audit depends on.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep a one-line enumerated red-flag list inline (it is well under the budget) or make the REFERENCE §Security read a required step in Phase 2 with a verifiable artefact.
